_comment: Desired state for the LoRa Basics Modem end devices reached over the
Basic Station gateway path. Applied by tools/apply-device-profiles.sh,
which creates or updates whatever is missing or stale, matching on name.
Basic Station is a gateway protocol, so nothing in here is Basic Station
specific. A device profile describes the end device that sits behind the
gateway, and for this stack that is the LoRa Basics Modem. If you put a
different Basic Station node on port 3001, give it its own profile.
The two profiles differ in LoRaWAN class, not in firmware. LBM ships as a
stack library with a board port on top (LBM-E is the same stack embedded in
an LR1121), so the regular and low-power builds share a MAC version, a set
of fPorts and a payload format, and a single profile would serve both. What
actually needs a second profile is Class C, because it changes what the
server may do: Class C keeps the receive window open, so downlinks, FUOTA,
remote multicast and ALC sync land without waiting for an uplink, at the
cost of the power budget that makes LBM's Class A worth using at all.
Pick the Class A profile unless the node is mains powered or the
application genuinely needs server-initiated downlinks.
LBM implements TS001-LoRaWAN L2 1.0.4 and RP2-1.0.3, so macVersion and
regParamsRevision below are not the ChirpStack UI defaults of 1.0.3 and A.
Class B is off in both: it has to be compiled in (LBM_CLASS_B) and needs
beacon synchronisation, which on LBM means running the ALC sync package.
ABP is off in both because LBM's ABP mode stores no non-volatile context,
so a reset means a new session that the server has never seen.
uplinkInterval 60 matches PERIODICAL_UPLINK_DELAY_S in the stock example.
ChirpStack only uses it to decide when a device counts as inactive, so it
does not have to match if your firmware differs.
tags are user-defined and are copied into every integration event of every
device using the profile, which is what makes them useful for filtering.

application.name: lora-basics-modem
application.description: LoRa Basics Modem end devices, reached through the Basic Station gateway path.

deviceProfiles.name: LoRa Basics Modem EU868 Class A
deviceProfiles.description: Default LBM build: OTAA, Class A, 60 s periodical uplink. The low-power choice.

deviceProfiles.name: LoRa Basics Modem EU868 Class C
deviceProfiles.description: Same stack in Class C, so the server can push downlinks, FUOTA and multicast without waiting for an uplink.
